turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.text:
**Exploring input patterns**

I'm considering demonstrating how each input pattern's zero voids can be represented as two, with a corresponding colored line starting from the left grid boundary and extending above the shape to its center-right edge. I'm curious about the directionality here. It might be possible to use the shape as a "window" and fill the voids with two. I'm exploring whether the entire thing represents a numeral pattern whose interior is just expanded. Maybe I need a demo to clarify the variable dimensions.

steps.name: ipython
steps.input: entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title="Continual-ARC task-64945636 pattern", content="For ARC task id task-64945636: identify each color-5 4-column glyph shaped by rows [1101,1001...,1111] (with one or more repeated middle [1001] rows). Fill all interior zeros between the left/right vertical boundaries in the middle rows and the top row's gap using color 2. Also add a horizontal color-2 beam on the row immediately above each glyph, from grid column 0 through the rightmost filled interior cell (one column left of the glyph's right boundary). Preserve all original 5s and zeros elsewhere. In the demo, glyph rows [1101,1001,1001,1111] got interior 2s and beam above ending at interior right column.", global_=True)
